ai.description: This frog reaches 4–6 cm. It is brown or grey with dark mottling and distinct skin flaps on the limbs. It features large, fully webbed feet and a pointed snout.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Kurixalus appendiculatus* is uniquely distinguished by the prominent, fleshy, triangular dermal appendage located at the heel of each hind limb.
ai.habitat: The Philippine Flying Frog inhabits tropical evergreen forests and moist deciduous woodlands, typically found at elevations ranging from near sea level up to 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: The Philippine flying frog is primarily nocturnal and uses its large, webbed feet to glide between trees, allowing it to escape predators or travel through the canopy.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Kurixalus appendiculatus* breeds during the monsoon, laying clutches of 20–50 eggs in foam nests attached to vegetation overhanging water bodies.
ai.distributionRemarks: In the Indian subcontinent, *Kurixalus appendiculatus* is found in Northeast India, primarily inhabiting tropical forests at elevations from sea level up to 1,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Philippine Flying Frog emits a series of high-pitched, insect-like chirps or whistles, typically heard from vegetation near forest streams or pools.
